HTEAM-CTX-G2.title: Project Juniper plan v3
HTEAM-CTX-G2.text:
Project Juniper - plan v3
Owner: Marcus Oyelaran. Last updated: 1 September 2026.

Goal
Replace the nightly Ledgerd batch invoicing job with an event-driven pipeline on the Stream bus, so usage shows up on a customer's draft invoice within 5 minutes instead of the next morning, with zero double-billing.

In scope
- Usage event consumers for metered products (API calls, seats, storage).
- Proration and plan-change handling for monthly and annual plans.
- Historical backfill of March-August usage events into the new store.
- Reconciliation tooling against Ledgerd during shadow mode.
- Cutover runbook and rollback procedure.

Out of scope
- Invoice PDF template redesign.
- Multi-currency discount rules (tracked separately by Revenue Engineering).
- Changes to the customer-facing billing page.
- Tax calculation logic (we call the existing tax provider as-is).

Milestones
M1 Event schema frozen - 21 Aug (done)
M2 Shadow run - 7 Sept to 18 Sept
M3 Cohort A cutover - 29 Sept
M4 Cohort B cutover - 13 Oct
M5 General cutover - 27 Oct
M6 Ledgerd decommission - 30 days after M5

Dependencies
- SRE (Ines Duarte): increase Stream bus partitions for the billing topic from 12 to 24 before M3. Requested 25 Aug, not yet scheduled.
- Tax team (Rafael Lindqvist): refresh tax provider sandbox credentials before the backfill dry run. Current credentials expire 20 Sept.
- Finance Ops (Siobhan Walsh): sign-off that the reconciliation diff is within the 0.1 percent tolerance before each cohort.
- Data Platform: no schema migrations on the usage warehouse during the week of each cutover.

RACI
Accountable: Marcus Oyelaran
Responsible: Hana Kobayashi (pipeline and proration), Tomas Reyes (backfill), Leila Farrokh (QA and reconciliation)
Consulted: Siobhan Walsh (Finance Ops), Rafael Lindqvist (Tax)
Informed: Grace Mbeki (Support lead), Dev Anand (Product)

Risks
R1 Month-end traffic spike overwhelms consumers. Likelihood medium, impact high. Mitigation: partition increase (SRE dependency); avoid any cutover in the last 3 days of a month.
R2 Backfill throttled by the tax provider rate limit. Likelihood medium, impact medium. Mitigation: run the backfill overnight, capped at 40 requests per second.
R3 Reconciliation diff does not reach tolerance. Likelihood low, impact high. Mitigation: extend the shadow run; do not cut over any cohort while the diff is above tolerance.
R4 Support unprepared for invoice questions. Likelihood medium, impact low. Mitigation: support briefing one week before each cohort.

Success measures
- Usage event to draft invoice line in under 5 minutes (p95).
- Reconciliation diff at or below 0.1 percent for two consecutive weeks before general cutover.
- Zero double-billed invoices.

Not covered in this plan
Budget, vendor costs and headcount are tracked by Marcus separately and are not part of this document.

HTEAM-CTX-G1.title: Juniper weekly sync notes, 8 September
HTEAM-CTX-G1.text:
Juniper weekly sync - notes
Date: Tuesday 8 September 2026, 10:00-10:45
Chair: Marcus Oyelaran (engineering manager)
Attendees: Hana Kobayashi (backend), Tomas Reyes (data engineering), Leila Farrokh (QA), Dev Anand (product), Siobhan Walsh (Finance Ops)
Notes taken by: Leila Farrokh

1. Shadow run results
The shadow run has been comparing new-pipeline invoices against Ledgerd output since 7 Sept. Reconciliation diff rate is 0.4 percent against the 0.1 percent target agreed with Finance Ops. Hana traced most of the diff to currency rounding in the proration path (mid-cycle plan changes on non-USD accounts). The remaining diffs look like timezone boundary issues on usage events stamped near midnight UTC.
Decision: extend the shadow run by one week. The shadow run now ends Friday 25 September instead of 18 September.

2. Cutover approach
Discussed big-bang versus staged. Siobhan and Leila both preferred staged, because Finance Ops cannot manually review more than about 300 invoices per day if something goes wrong.
Decision: cutover will be done by customer cohort, not all at once. Cohort A is internal accounts plus 40 friendly customers, then Cohort B (roughly 2,000 accounts on monthly plans), then everyone else. Dates per the plan, adjusted for the shadow-run extension - Marcus to update the plan.

3. Scope
Dev raised that Design has been mocking up a new invoice PDF layout.
Decision: the invoice PDF redesign is out of scope for Juniper and moves to the Q1 backlog. Dev to tell Design.

4. Rollback
Decision: keep Ledgerd running in read-only mode for 30 days after the final cohort is cut over, so any invoice can be regenerated from the old system if needed.

5. Pricing-table freeze
Siobhan asked whether pricing-table changes should be frozen during cutover. Not decided. Siobhan to check with Revenue and bring an answer to the next sync (15 Sept).

6. Go/no-go sign-off
Open question: who signs off on the Cohort A go/no-go. Marcus suggested Dev; Dev suggested Finance Ops should, since they own the reconciliation tolerance. Left open.

Risks raised
- Stream bus consumer lag spikes at month end. Tomas saw 11 minutes of lag on 31 August with the current 12 partitions.
- The tax provider API is rate limited to 50 requests per second; the historical backfill may get throttled if it runs alongside live traffic.
- Leila is on PTO 28 Sept - 2 Oct, which overlaps the planned Cohort A window. No QA backup named yet.

Action items
- Hana: fix currency rounding in the proration path. Due Thursday 17 Sept.
- Tomas: backfill script for March-August usage events; dry run on staging by 22 Sept.
- Leila: reconciliation dashboard showing diff rate by cohort. Due 21 Sept.
- Dev: tell Design the PDF redesign moved to Q1; update the roadmap page.
- Siobhan: ask Revenue about a pricing-table freeze; answer at the 15 Sept sync.
- Marcus: confirm on-call coverage for cutover weekend with the SRE lead (Ines Duarte); update plan dates.

Next sync: Tuesday 15 September.

- Introduced Pact contract tests between 5 internal services, cutting integration-environment breakages from roughly 9 per month to 2.
- Implemented field-level encryption for patient phone numbers using envelope keys in AWS KMS.

Brindlecap Labs | Junior Developer | Cincinnati, OH | Aug 2020 - Jul 2021

- Wrote the product's first automated test suite, taking line coverage from 0% to 71%.
- Handled customer-support escalations one day per week.

SIDE PROJECT
Sparrowhawk (open source, maintainer since 2022)
- Go library for idempotency keys backed by PostgreSQL advisory locks; about 640 GitHub stars.
- Supports configurable key expiry and a replay-safe response cache; test suite runs against PostgreSQL 13 through 16.

EDUCATION
Ohio Valley Polytechnic University | B.S. Computer Science, Minor in Mathematics | May 2020
- Senior capstone: a route-planning simulator for municipal snowplow fleets.

SKILLS
Languages: Go, Kotlin, Python, SQL, some TypeScript
Data and messaging: PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, AWS SQS
Infrastructure: AWS (ECS, RDS, KMS), Terraform, Docker, GitHub Actions, Datadog
Practices: design docs, transactional outbox, idempotency, contract testing, on-call and runbooks

PI-A:JD.title: the job description the user is targeting
PI-A:JD.text:
SENIOR BACKEND ENGINEER, PAYMENTS & LEDGER
Tallowmarket, Inc. | Denver, CO

ABOUT TALLOWMARKET
Tallowmarket is a B2B marketplace where independent restaurants buy directly from regional farms and ranches. Our Payments & Ledger group moves about $1.1B a year through escrowed payouts to more than 6,500 growers. We are a team of 140 people, about 55 of them in engineering. Our backend is Go on PostgreSQL, with Kafka between services and Temporal for long-running payment workflows.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Own services in the money path: escrow holds, split payouts to growers, refunds and chargebacks.
- Design and evolve Harrow, our double-entry ledger built on PostgreSQL, as volume grows from 400,000 to a projected 1.5 million ledger entries per day.
- Improve the reliability of the nightly settlement batch that runs at 02:00 Mountain Time and must finish before banks open.
- Lead technical design reviews and mentor mid-level engineers on the team.
- Join the on-call rotation, currently one week in six.
- Partner with Finance and Risk on reconciliation and audit requirements.

WHAT YOU BRING
- 5+ years of professional backend experience in Go, Java or Kotlin.
- Deep PostgreSQL knowledge: indexing, locking, isolation levels, and safe online migrations.
- Experience with event-driven systems (Kafka, Kinesis or similar) and idempotent processing.
- A track record of leading multi-engineer projects from design doc to launch.
- Clear written communication; we make most decisions in design docs.

NICE TO HAVE
- Prior work on a double-entry ledger or a payments platform.
- Experience reducing PCI DSS scope.
- Stripe Connect or Adyen for Platforms integration experience.
- Experience with Temporal or another durable workflow engine.

WORK ARRANGEMENT
Hybrid: in our Denver LoDo office Tuesday through Thursday; Monday and Friday are flexible. Relocation assistance is available for candidates moving to the Denver metro area.

COMPENSATION
Base salary band: $172,000 - $208,000 USD, plus equity and a 6% 401(k) match. This role is leveled at L5 (Senior).

INTERVIEW PROCESS
Recruiter screen (30 minutes), a 60-minute ledger design exercise, a Go coding session, and a values conversation with our Director of Engineering, Imani Castellanos.

Tallowmarket is an equal opportunity employer.

items.question: Hold on, I thought we agreed last week to cut everyone over at once and drop the cohort idea. Why are we still talking about cohorts?
items.answer: We did discuss big-bang versus staged, and the decision went the other way. The notes from the 8 September sync record that cutover will be done by customer cohort, not all at once, with Cohort A being internal accounts plus 40 friendly customers, then Cohort B, then everyone else. The reason staged won was that Finance Ops can't manually review more than about 300 invoices a day if something goes wrong. So the cohort idea is still live, and Marcus is updating the plan dates to account for the shadow-run extension.

items.question: Did we decide last week whether pricing-table changes are frozen during cutover? If we did, who made the call, and give me the one line I should say to the group about it.
items.answer:
No, that one wasn't decided. Siobhan raised whether pricing-table changes should be frozen during cutover, and the notes record it as **not decided**, with Siobhan checking with Revenue and bringing an answer to the next sync on 15 September. So there's no call and no owner to name yet.

The line to say: "Pricing-table freeze during cutover is still open, Siobhan is checking with Revenue and we'll have an answer at the 15 September sync."

items.role: USER: a team member or lead in a meeting. OTHER PARTY: colleagues. Natively: constructive words for the user in the meeting.
items.question: We've got one sprint and three things on the table: the proration rounding bug, the reconciliation dashboard, and the flaky integration tests. Which one do you think goes first?
items.answer: The proration rounding bug goes first. It's the one that touches money customers can see, so every day it's open is a day we're shipping wrong numbers, and that's the kind of thing that erodes trust fast. The dashboard and the flaky tests matter, but they're not producing incorrect output in front of users. If the bug turns out to be deeper than expected, I'd want to know that early so we can decide whether to timebox the fix or ship a stopgap.

items.role: USER: a team member or lead in a meeting. OTHER PARTY: colleagues. Natively: constructive words for the user in the meeting.
items.question: You've done a billing migration like this somewhere before, right? What bit you last time?
items.answer: Honestly, the part that always bites is the data, not the code. Old records that don't map cleanly, duplicate subscriptions, and invoices that were already paid under the old system. So I'd reconcile first, run both systems side by side for a cycle, and only then cut over.
